sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Body dark brown to black, antennae, mouthparts and legs yellowish brown, intersegmental membranes whitish, wings dark yellowish brown. Setae on the head sparse, denser on the pronotum and the wings. Head broad, pear-shaped, compound eyes distinctly projecting, almost hemispherical. Postclypeus raised like a cushion, and the frons behind it transversely depressed as far as the anterior margin of the ocelli; the frons behind the ocelli flat, slightly sunken. Fontanelle appearing as a bright streak, surrounded by several very faint concentric lines, with a weak ridge-like swelling in front of it. Compound eyes large and almost hemispherical, but distinctly shorter than the temple (the distance from the posterior margin of the compound eye to the end of the sagittal suture about twice the diameter of the compound eye). Ocelli large, directed obliquely forward, their inner margin raised, the distance to the compound eye equal to their long diameter — a good character for distinguishing it from related species. Antenna 15-segmented, segment 3 distinctly longer than segment 2, segment 4 about as long as segment 2. Pronotum much narrower than the head, anterior margin nearly straight, posterior margin almost not concave; the surface deeply depressed on both sides behind the anterior margin, so that the anterior margin is raised and projecting, especially in the middle, this swelling extending backward along the midline. Wings long and broad, dark yellowish brown.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Two soldier morphs (major and minor), differing less than in the Javanese L. batavus, the author suspecting a difference in nest age only. Body brownish black; head almost black, the nasus concolorous, slightly paler only at the very apex at the opening of the gland; antennae and legs brown, tibiae and tarsi distinctly paler than the femora. Dorsum of body and head hairless, with only a few setae at the tip of the nasus. Head pear-shaped in dorsal view, in lateral view concave above the base of the nasus, so that the frontal outline is distinctly depressed. Antenna 14-segmented, segment 2 short, segment 3 about one and a half times as long as segment 2, segment 4 distinctly longer than segment 2. Pronotum small, neither anterior nor posterior margin concave, the anterior margin moderately raised.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Three worker morphs, the largest darkest, almost as dark as the soldier, the smaller ones paler. Head oval in all morphs, longer than wide, fontanelle distinct, more than twice as long as wide; in the major worker the boundaries of the fontanelle are very distinct, in the minor worker the boundary lines are diffuse. Antenna 15-segmented in all morphs, but the length of the basal segments very variable: in the minor and medium workers segment 2 is more or less longer than segment 3 (longest in the minor worker, where segment 2 is also thicker and more strongly chitinized), whereas in the major worker segment 2 is distinctly shorter than segment 3.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Measurements (mm). Alate: body length with wings 18.00—21.00, body length without wings 9.25, fore wing length 16.50—19.00, head width 2.01, pronotum width 1.52—1.73, pronotum length 0.92—0.95, compound eye length 0.53—0.56. Major soldier: body length 4.61—5.00, head length including nasus 1.80—2.01, head length (without nasus) 1.16—1.27, head width 1.13—1.20, pronotum width 0.62—0.68. Minor soldier: body length 4.04, head length including mandibles 1.73, head length (without mandibles) 1.09, head width 0.99, pronotum width 0.53. Major worker: body length 5.00—5.3, head length 1.69—1.87, head width 1.31—1.45, pronotum width 0.74—0.81. Medium worker: body length 4.60—4.81, head length 1.45—1.48, head width 1.16—1.20, pronotum width 0.63—0.65. Minor worker: body length 3.36, head length 1.13, head width 0.88, pronotum width 0.51. Type locality Fort de Kock, Sumatra, first collected by Jacobson in 1924, in spherical nests; alates were collected in October 1925 (month 10).

note: Adapted from the original description by Kemner (1930), original in German; the alate, the soldier (two morphs) and the worker (three morphs) are all described and measured. The genus name appears on the page as "Lacessititermes"; in the discussion the Javanese specimens of atrior and sordidus are combined into one species.
